title: CumulusCompute - Redwood Partner Intro
summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood AE/SE and CumulusCompute infra + product leads to scope a partner pilot. Key themes: joint go-to-market, network connectivity options (VPC peering vs Private Link), support for private deployments, preferred GPU SKUs, SSO/KMS/audit needs. Action items and next steps agreed: share security pack and pilot TnC, schedule kernel/benchmark run in two weeks, follow-up on pricing model for dedicated pools.
next_steps: Redwood to send Security & SOC2 docs + network checklist (Maya) - by 2026-10-13
Cumulus to share sample workload/throughput targets and dataset size (Priya) - by 2026-10-15
Schedule kernel benchmark run with Diego and Alex - week of 2026-10-25
Draft pilot MOU and estimated dedicated commit options (Maya) - by 2026-10-20

Priya Rao: Share representative request traces and dataset sizes (2026-10-15)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-11 16:00 PST
Duration: 48 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Cumulus Head of Infra), Tom (CTO), Alex (Cloud Architect), Sara (Biz Ops)

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do intros quick and then dive into what a partner pilot could look like, diego and i are with redwood inference, i'm maya, ae, and diego is our se.
00:18 Tom: thanks maya, we are excited, i'll hand it to priya to kick off our goals.
00:24 Priya: yeah hi all, at cumulus we run a multi-tenant cloud infra, we want to evaluate partner integrations for managed inference — primary interest is GPU offering + a managed control plane we can white-label. main blockers: network isolation, key management, and predictable latency for LLMs used by our customers.
00:42 Maya: perfect, that's exactly the scope we usually start with. diego can you give a quick runtime overview?
00:48 Diego: sure, so redwood is a serving runtime optimized for throughput and low tail latency, we do continuous batching, kv cache, and quantization-friendly execution paths. side note, our kernel selector picks optimal kernels based on seqlength distribution, that matters a lot for cost.
01:10 Alex: quick q — for private deployment do we need to open outbound or is there an option for fully air-gapped control plane?
01:18 Diego: good question — our private customer model has two options: a private control plane with customer-managed VPC peering (no egress of model data to public internet) or fully on-prem packaged deployments. the control plane needs limited outbound for metrics by default but we do a mode for offline/air-gapped installs. sometimes the naming in the docs gets garbled — we call it Redwood Private or "Redwood Private runtime" in our docs.
01:40 Priya: ok sounds promising. how do you handle kms? we need customer-managed keys and hsm support.
01:46 Maya: we support KMS integrations — customer-managed CMKs via cloud kms providers and HSM integrations for enterprise. our audit logs include token-level tracing, we can redact or not store inputs depending on config.
02:05 Tom: on the infra side, what's the typical gpu sku you run? we run a mix of A100s and newer h100 equivalents across zones.
02:14 Diego: we support a broad matrix — a100, h100, and some partners with next-gen chips. for cost-sensitive workloads quantized 4-bit runs on cheaper instances, but for low-latency larger seq lengths h100 or fp16 paths get better tail latency. also batching policy is tunable per route.
02:35 Priya: how does routing work — can we steer traffic regionally or by tier?
02:40 Diego: yes, smart routing by policy — latency, cost, region, customer tier. we can also fallback to compatible model variants when capacity's constrained. this is useful during bursts.
02:55 Alex: if we wanted a joint offering where cumulus supplies gpu infra and redwood supplies the control plane + runtime, is that a supported partner flow?
03:03 Maya: absolutely — that's the partner dedicated flow. we usually do a pilot: dedicated GPU pools, set autoscale policy, SLA targets, and then tie in billing/commits. we can white-label console elements for partners too.
03:20 Sara: product/ops question — how invasive is the integration on our side? we want minimal touch for tenants.
03:27 Diego: depends — private control plane with peering is light on tenant changes; we can expose an API or an S3-backed model registry. the more seamless option is running our dedicated runtime in your VPC with minimal tenant-side config.
03:45 Priya: can you share perf benchmarks? we need to see p95 latency at our expected throughput.
03:51 Maya: yes we'll share benchmark artifacts — diego will run a kernel selection and sample run with your traces. please send the sample workload.
04:00 Tom: any compliance concerns — SOC2/ISO? we need to include those in our vendor assessment.
04:06 Maya: we have SOC2 Type II, and can provide the attestation and security pack; for enterprise deals we do more extensive security questionnaires and can provide network diagrams and audit log examples.
04:20 Priya: great. pricing — do you do per-token or per-instance? we want committed pricing for our dedicated pool.
04:27 Maya: hosted we do usage-based per-token/embedding; for dedicated we do reserved capacity contracts with monthly/annual commits. the SKU depends on GPU type and any quantization/throughput guarantees — we'll draft options.
04:42 Alex: one more deep tech — how do you manage kv cache when requests are coming from multiple tenants? cache isolation?
04:50 Diego: yes, cache is tenant-isolated; we support prefix caching and a per-tenant cache granularity. there are tradeoffs with memory — we can tune eviction and sharding.
05:05 Priya: potential concern — if we route many small requests, batching could introduce latency. can we set strict SLOs?
05:12 Diego: yes, batching has a max latency window; you can set SLOs and we will respect hard latency caps for specific routes, trading off throughput.
05:25 Tom: what about model updates and versioning for tenants? we need rollback and canary.
05:30 Maya: rollouts are first-class: canary deploys, A/B tests, automatic fallback policies. we also keep model versions pinned per tenant.
05:40 Sara: ok for go-to-market, do you co-sell? referral? revenue share?
05:45 Maya: typical partner packs include co-marketing, referral credits, and for deep integrations we can discuss revenue share on dedicated deals. that's negotiable.
05:58 Alex: any references for other cloud partners?
06:02 Maya: yes we have a few partner case studies — i'll share links in the follow-up.
06:10 Priya: wonder about support model — on-call & escalation.
06:14 Maya: we offer enterprise SLAs with on-call support and a designated CSM for pilots.
06:22 Diego: technical note — to validate perf we'll need a kernel/benchmark run. ideally you provide traces + a small dataset to run replicable tests.
06:35 Priya: can you do a small PoC where we bring 2 racks of gpus and we run your control plane?
06:40 Maya: yes, that's a normal pilot. we'll scope throughput targets and a short-term reserved capacity.
06:48 Tom: timeline — we'd like pilot live in 4-6 weeks. feasible?
06:52 Diego: technically yes, if we get the network & workload details this week, we can prep benchmarks and a pilot image.
07:00 Maya: recap — action items: maya send security pack; priya send traces; diego plan benchmarks; alex check firewall rules. we'll follow up with a pilot MOU.
07:12 Tom: thanks everyone, we'll review internally and get back.
07:18 Maya: thanks, i'll follow up with meeting notes and links.

Post-call notes:
- Shared link placeholders during call: security pack (link), partner playbook deck (link), benchmark template spreadsheet (link)
- Customer stressed need for HSM/CMK and private deployment options; also asked for explicit p95 latency numbers for 4-bit quantized vs fp16 paths.
- Next meeting: schedule kernel benchmark week of 2026-10-25.
